original_card.question: Can a legal decoder or coframe change improve the full signed moment, including changed helper targets?
methods: Construct and independently check one source-bound instance of the stated first experiment.
Seek an exact counterexample or target-specific complete-budget obstruction to that same proposed change.
original_card.acceptance_gate: A source-bound arbitrary-input identity and legal producer/consumer boundary with the complete paid and productive target invoice, including restoration, ownership, native alignment and extra charges. Price under the actual current model; historical ceiling.py assumptions must be established before use. A favorable optimistic relaxation keeps a route open but is not a completed supplier. A scoped local result remains useful; expansion requires the family-level budget gate.

first_step.inspect: Read revision 8, the selected review and live exact-source handoffs. Then follow this card's bounded first_experiment.
first_step.scope: Source-bound orientation only, not a supplier replay or theorem proof.

original_card.first_experiment: Price one complete changed itinerary with both paid and productive histograms. Check #5693/#5698 for overlap and their exact hypotheses before another coframe search. Use the signed invoice preflight where its boundary contract agrees; an inconclusive concave comparison is not a power crossing. Stop if an optimistic complete budget fails at the chosen target or native delivery remains unspecified.
original_card.bottleneck_link: Judge the actual current supplier contract and complete signed target/paid bill; frozen-profile ceilings require an applicability proof.
allowed_variations: One exact source head, helper/cut region or quantified proposition and changed hypothesis; check live handoffs first. Different seeds are not different scopes.
scope_change_triggers: Changing source head, helper/cut domain, operation alphabet or caller boundary without recording the new scope.
Treating an archived proposal or local numerical pass as complete supplier admission.

existing_checks.scope: Selected PR5599: complete helper-subspace construction and independent caller replay; five framework assumptions remain.
existing_checks.remaining: The next experiment must identify uncovered source-specific work. Successor archive intake does not transfer this admission.

actual_scope: Global all-field lower bound 36732955/262144 = 140.1251 (hence 141) on the additive full-plane COPY mass of every finite scalar decoder of the strict 112-port PR1825/PR1889 mask, under CubeJerry's #4365 tariff. It is a new 425-clique feasible point of PR5560's clique programme, checked exactly on all 39,087^2 ordered span pairs. PR5560's Lemmas 1-3 are reused unchanged.
scope_change_reason: The card asks for a legal decoder or coframe change that improves the full signed moment. This package instead raises a lower bound on one decoder family's COPY mass: it answers Open next question 2 of PR5560 (research/plane-port-global-rank-dual), the stronger clique-programme certificate. It narrows the plane-port break-even window from [140, 164] to [141, 164].
bottleneck_link: Side result for the plane-port coverage lever (plane-port-copy-budgets). A decoder must cost at most about 160-164 per call to break even with the incumbent word. The all-field floor rises from 140 to 141, which shrinks that window by one unit. No kappa change.
stop_rule: Stop at the first exact certificate above 140 (floor 141); further column generation is left as an open question.
evidence: verify.py: independent closure census of 39,087 generated subspaces, tariffs cross-checked by Gaussian elimination on 4,000 random pairs, 425 clique columns, exact feasibility on all 1,527,793,569 ordered pairs (minimum slack 0, attained exactly on the 1,732 zero-tariff pairs), bound 36732955/262144, and four rejecting controls including PR5560's own certificate (139.11 < 140). generate/ holds the row-and-column generation and rounding code (scipy HiGHS); it is not needed for the proof.
author: Nick Petalas
ai_assistance: Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed.

open_questions.question: What is the optimum of the full clique programme, and does it exceed 164?
open_questions.why_it_matters: A certified value above 164 would close the plane-port lever for every coefficient field in #4365's contract without settling the 224 conjecture.
open_questions.first_step: Continue generate/colgen.py past the 140 stop (raise STOP), and replace the local-search pricing with an exact MILP pricer to obtain a certified upper bound on the programme.
open_questions.blocked_by: Local-search pricing slowed to fewer than ten new columns per round near 140; no exact pricing bound is available yet.

open_questions.question: Can columns other than cliques (C5 covers, three- and four-plane rank duals) beat the clique programme's optimum?
open_questions.why_it_matters: PR5560 estimates the clique programme at about 167, which leaves little headroom above 164.
open_questions.first_step: Add the sharp C5 covers of c5-residual-weighted-cover as columns, with the same exhaustive span-pair separation used by verify.py.
open_questions.blocked_by: Nothing; the separation step takes about 15 seconds on one machine.
